title: iPhone Duo: The five most important things you need to know
content:
Macworld





After years of rumors, leaks, and speculation, the folding iPhone is finally here. This project has been reported on for so long that our first article about it dates to 2018! Its name is iPhone Duo—not iPhone Ultra as previously expected—and there will be a lot to say about it over the coming weeks before and after its release on October 23.
But for now, here are the five most important things you need to know about iPhone Duo.
$1,999, two colors, mid-October
As expected, the iPhone Duo is about twice the price of an iPhone 17 Pro. The starting price is $1,999 with 256GB of storage, which is actually on the lower side of the rumors. Adding more storage inflates the price, with options up to 2 terabytes for $3,199.
Preorders start on October 16, and the iPhone Duo goes on sale on October 23.
There are two colors available: Star White and Night Sky. These are very similar to the Silver and Midnight colors we’ve seen in previous Apple products.

				
					

				
			
Apple




It’s all about flexibility
One thing the rumors didn’t pick up on: Both the inner and outer displays have the same aspect ratio: 1:1.4. That makes the outer display exactly one half of the inner display, and Apple uses this symmetry, along with a lot of orientation sensing, to alter the way iOS works.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Currently, many iOS apps, and the operating system itself, do not adjust to multiple orientations. With the Duo, Apple has updated its own apps to work in portrait or landscape, and even behave differently depending on whether they’re on the outside or inside screen.

				
					

				
			The inner display shows two home screens at once, and the dock is on the side.
Apple




The Dock now runs up the side of the screen, allowing more vertical room for the Home Screen, and the inside display simply shows two home screens at once. Most app toolbars and controls are also now on the side edge, along with a new more compact status icon area.
Speakers are on the top and bottom, so no matter which way you hold the iPhone Duo, open or closed, you get proper sound orientation and stereo separation.

				
					

				
			
Apple




The trick is that apps can adapt to present themselves to both the dual-screen nature and shifting orientations of iPhone Duo. You can show your FaceTime call on the outer display as well as the inside, so other people can see and participate in the call. You can partially fold the phone and use it that way and the interface reacts. Fold it like a tent and it goes into Standby mode to show big clock, calendar, photo, and weather widgets–even when you’re not charging. Apple even showed a quick glimpse of the Duo acting like a tiny laptop with touchscreen keys.

				
					

				
			Fold the Duo over and it goes into Standby mode, even when not charging.
Apple




And of course, you can run two apps side by side, or even two instances of the same app in some cases. Plus, you can save “married” apps for easy access later. And later this year, you’ll even be able to use the USB-C Apple Pencil on both the inner and outer displays.
The focus is on letting you use both the inner and outer displays in all sorts of flexible ways.
A new camera experience
The two outside cameras are 48 megapixel wide and ultra-wide. It’s not the new variable-aperture camera of the iPhone 18 Pro and there’s no telephoto, as expected. But there are a few software tricks up Apple’s sleeve.
iPhone Duo reacts to being propped up or folded in various ways to let you do unique things, like take selfies with the outside cameras while it is unfolded, using the outer display to show you the shot.
Fold it halfway to prop the camera up and step back to take shots with the new Smart Take feature that automatically takes the shot when everyone is posed and ready instead of relying on a strict timer.

				
					

				
			You can  mirror your FaceTime call to the outer display so others can participate, too.
Apple




And the new FaceTime camera on the inside is now under the display, so it disappears entirely when you’re not using it.
There’s even a new Kid Cue feature that plays Peanuts animations on the outer display to grab your child’s attention, so they looks at the camera when you’re trying to take their picture.
A focus on durability and display quality
Apple has clearly heard complaints about other folding phones and has given Duo a polished titanium frame, and an ultra-precise hinge design using over 100 elements. Embedded magnets give you that satisfying “click” when you close it and keep it shut.
The result is an IP68 water and dust rating, which is a lot better than we’ve seen from most other foldable phones and equivalent to other recent iPhones.

				
					

				
			Apple spent years perfecting the Duo’s hinge.
Apple




Apple went to great lengths to highlight the superiority of its inner display. It uses a new nano-texture matte finish that helps make the crease harder to notice, and a multi-layer bonding process for durability and to make the display fully flat so you don’t get that annoying waviness or creasing you sometimes see with foldable phones.

				
					

				
			The multiple display layers slide past each other like pages on a book, to reduce warping and waves.
Apple




A20 Pro and C2 modem, and battery life
The A20 Pro is at the heart of the iPhone Duo, and it’s just like the one in the iPhone 18 Pro–there aren’t any disabled GPU cores or anything like that.
Sustained performance will be a little lower because cooling the chip is more challenging, but it will still be much faster than the iPhone 17 Pro—up to 35% higher sustained performance, according to Apple.
Like the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone Duo also includes both Apple’s N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, and the new C2 modem. Apple says the new modem provides better reliability and efficiency, 50 percent faster uploads, and supports mmWave in the United States.
Both halves of the iPhone Fold have a high-density battery, which gives it very good battery life specs. Apple says you can expect up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display, and 31 hours on the inner display. That falls right in between the battery life of an iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, and is quite a bit longer than the iPhone Air.
And yes, MagSafe and Qi wireless charging are still supported.

title: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo Feature Apple's New C2 Modem [Updated]
content:
Apple today unveiled new iPhone 18 Pro models and the iPhone Duo – the company's first foldable iPhone – and both the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo feature Apple's new custom-designed C2 modem for 5G connectivity.


Prior to today's announcements, there was speculation that Apple's C2 in-house modem would not support mmWave 5G in the U.S., and that the company would once again rely on Qualcomm to fill the gap for American carriers. Apparently, that's not the case, at least as far mmWave support goes.

Apple's press release for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and the tech specs page for the two models appear to indicate that the C2 modem is limited to only the smaller iPhone 18 Pro model, leaving the iPhone 18 Pro Max on Qualcomm modems. The reason for the distinction is unclear given the near identical capabilities of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

Apple says the C2 brings AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability, and now supports mmWave in the U.S. The company claims the C2 also delivers meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy.

As for mmWave support, Apple's U.S. specifications list bands n258, n260, and n261, alongside sub-6GHz 5G with 4×4 MIMO, but the UK specifications list sub-6GHz only.

Meanwhile, both models feature the N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support.

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max come in burgundy, glacier, silver, and black colors, with prices starting at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively. Both models come in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB storage options and will be available to order September 12.

iPhone Duo is available in star white and night sky colors, and starts at $1,999, coming in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, and 2TB storage capacities. Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo begin on Friday, October 16, with availability beginning Friday, October 23.

Update: This article originally stated that all three models include the C2 modem, but it appears the iPhone 18 Pro Max does not in fact include it.

title: 5 really cool things about the new AirPods 5
content:
Macworld





Apple introduced the AirPods 5 during its Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday. Apple’s popular earphones have a very similar design to the model they replace, but they feature several internal improvements over the AirPods 4. Here are five things you need to know about the new AirPods 5.


1. Better Active Noise Cancellation
Apple introduced Active Noise Cancellation to the entry-level AirPods with the AirPods 4 in 2024, a welcome feature for anyone who prefers open-air earphones instead of in-ear ones such as the AirPods Pro. On the AirPods 5, the ANC has gotten even better, thanks to a “new multi-port acoustic architecture and improved computational audio algorithms.” Apple claims that the AirPods 5 removes up to 50 percent more noise compared to the AirPods 4.
Apple also improved Transparency mode so that voices and sounds are more natural. The Adaptive Audio feature tracks the sound in your environment and automatically switches between ANC and Transparency modes.


						

							


2. Active Noise Cancellation is now standard
Active Noise Cancellation is now a standard feature for the AirPods, meaning you can’t get a model without it, as was the case with AirPods 4. So you no longer have to shop and ponder if you really need ANC or not–if you don’t want to use it, then simply turn it off.


						

							


3. Improved sound quality
That new multiport acoustic architecture that improved ANC also works with a “next-generation Adaptive EQ” to generate better sound across “an even wider range of ear geometries,” according to Apple’s announcement. This also makes Personalized Spatial Audio sound more immersive.

				
					

				
			
Apple made improvements that result in better sound from the AirPods 5.

Apple



							


4. Better battery life
The AirPods 5 are rated at 5 hours of playback with ANC active, which is one hour longer than the AirPods 4. Combined with the charging case, the AirPods 5 offer 22 hours of battery life when using ANC, a two-hour boost over the AirPods 4.


						

							


5. The price
The AirPods 5 with a USB-C charging case is $129, which is the same as the AirPods 4 without ANC, effectively a $50 price cut over AirPods 4 with ANC. In this era of increasing prices, this is a great surprise.
One caveat, however. The $129 AirPods now come with a wired charging case, which means you need to plug it in to charge it. If that’s a nuisance, Apple offers the AirPods 5 with a wireless charging case for $149 (and you’ll also get volume controls built into the stems like AirPods Pro). So, the AirPods 5 (with ANC standard) and the wireless charging case are still $30 cheaper than the AirPods 4 with ANC. Cool.


						

							




The AirPods 5 are available for pre-order now, with shipments starting on September 18.

title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide: Everything you need to know about the new iPhones
content:
Macworld





Apple has unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. They retain the 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch screen sizes and aluminium unibody design introduced with the previous generation, but Apple has made substantial changes to the cameras, processor, cooling, battery life and connectivity.
The biggest camera upgrade is a new 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, which can automatically move between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4 depending on lighting and depth of field. Apple says the widest aperture delivers around 50% better low-light performance, while new Pro controls add manual aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram controls.
Inside is the A20 Pro, Apple’s first iPhone chip made using a 2nm process. It has a new six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50% more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro. A larger vapor chamber and new M-series-inspired chip packaging also improve heat dissipation, with Apple claiming up to 40% better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro.
The other major changes are battery life of up to 36 hours on the Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max, faster wired charging, the new Apple-designed C2 cellular modem, and a redesigned Dynamic Island capable of showing three Live Activities simultaneously. 
iPhone 18 Pro/Max vs iPhone 17 Pro/Max: Top 10 changes at a glance
The five biggest changes are the variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, longer battery life and redesigned Dynamic Island/connectivity system. Here is an overview of what’s new compared to the previous generation.  


FeatureiPhone 18 Pro / Pro MaxiPhone 17 Pro / Pro MaxWhat’s changed

Main camera48MP, variable ƒ/1.48–ƒ/4 aperture48MP, fixed apertureMajor new photographic control
ProcessorA20 Pro, 2nmA19 ProNew manufacturing process
GPU7-core, up to 40% faster6-coreSignificant graphics boost

Apple has added a 2TB option to the smaller Pro for the first time, while retaining 256GB as the entry-level capacity.


iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Max release date: When will the new iPhones go on sale?
The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max were announced on Wednesday, September 9, 2026.
Pre-orders start at 5 a.m. Pacific on Saturday, September 12. That’s 1pm in the U.K.

Pre-order iPhone 18 Pro and Max at Apple U.K. 
Both models will then go on sale on Friday, September 18, 2026 in more than 65 countries and regions. Another 20 countries will get the phones from September 25.
You will be able to buy the phones directly from Apple online or at Apple Stores, as well as through mobile networks and authorized Apple retailers. Apple sells unlocked iPhones directly through its website and stores.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			
This is the Burgundy variant (we think Deep Cherry was a much nicer name).

Apple




The iPhone 18 Pro retains the aluminium unibody introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, as well as the Ceramic Shield on the rear and Ceramic Shield 2 over the display. The camera system remains arranged on the large raised plateau across the upper part of the rear casing.
Screen sizes are unchanged at 6.3 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro and 6.9 inches for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, both using Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz.
Apple offers four finishes this year:
Burgundy 
Glacier
Silver
Black
That means Cosmic Orange and Deep Blue disappear, while black returns to the Pro line despite pre-launch reports suggesting it would not.
The pre-event leaks suggested the basic chassis dimensions would remain very close to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, with the camera plateau rather than the body itself becoming thicker. 
The new iPhones share the same screen sizes and overall form as their predecessors, but both models are slightly heavier this time. 
iPhone 18 Pro dimensions: 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm / 5.91 x 2.83 x 0.34 in

Changes to the Dynamic Island
Apple has redesigned the Dynamic Island. Apple says new display technology creates additional usable space and allows the Dynamic Island to display up to three Live Activities at once, for example navigation, music and a sports score.
Apple has not announced fully under-display Face ID. Pre-launch reports suggested that one or more infrared Face ID components could move beneath the OLED panel, allowing the notch to shrink, but Apple hasn’t confirmed the underlying sensor arrangement.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cameras: Are the cameras the same?

				
					

				
			
The iPhone 18 Pro cameras.

Apple




Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have the same three-camera rear system. The main change is not resolution—all three remain 48MP—but the new variable-aperture Main camera and new computational imaging pipeline.
The three most notable camera upgrades are:
Variable aperture on the 48MP Main camera.
A new Main camera sensor and imaging pipeline, improving low-light performance and detail.
More extensive manual Pro controls, including aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram.


						

							




Rear cameras


CameraResolutionFocal lengthAperturePixel information
Fusion Main48MP24mm / 48mm, 1x / 2xƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, ƒ/4 variable2.44μm quad-pixel / 1.22μm individual
Fusion Ultra Wide48MP13mm, 0.5x / macroƒ/2.21.4μm quad-pixel / 0.7μm individual
Fusion Telephoto48MP100mm / 200mm, 4x / 8xƒ/2.81.4μm quad-pixel / 0.7μm individual

 



The Main camera’s six-blade mechanical aperture can automatically open to ƒ/1.48 in low light or close as far as ƒ/4 for increased depth of field. Apple says the widest setting improves low-light performance by around 50%. Photographers can also select aperture manually.
Both Pro models also offer up to 8x optical-quality zoom from the Telephoto camera. Contrary to some earlier rumors, the variable-aperture camera is not exclusive to the Pro Max.


Front camera
Apple has retained the 18MP Center Stage front camera, rather than moving to the rumored 24MP sensor. It supports automatic reframing, Center Stage, ultra-stabilized video and Dual Capture.
The front camera remains visibly associated with the Dynamic Island. Apple has not announced an under-display selfie camera on the iPhone 18 Pro.
iPhone 18 Pro video changes
Frame rates: Cinematic effects can now be applied after shooting to ordinary videos captured at up to 60fps. The phones continue to offer 4K 120fps Dolby Vision for high-frame-rate shooting.
Time-lapse: Time-lapse receives a significant upgrade to 4K with Dolby Vision HDR.
Computational photography: Apple has introduced a new imaging pipeline, smart focus tracking, improved Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, an Extend tool and Photographic Styles 3, which adds texture and grain adjustments.


						

							


A20 Pro processor: How fast is it?

				
					

				
			
Apple has redesigned the iPhone chip. 

Apple




Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max use Apple’s new A20 Pro processor.
It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, down from the 3nm-class process used for A19 Pro, giving Apple more scope to improve efficiency and transistor density.
The chip includes:
6-core CPU
7-core GPU
Neural Accelerators integrated into the CPU/GPU architecture
Dual 16-core Neural Engine, 32 cores in total
50% more memory bandwidth than A19 Pro
Apple says the GPU is up to 40% faster than A19 Pro, while the Neural Engine offers roughly double the AI processing capability.
One particularly important change is the packaging. Inspired by Apple’s M-series Mac chips, A20 Pro places the processor die side-by-side with memory rather than stacking memory directly in the chip’s thermal path. This improves heat transfer and allows the processor to couple more directly to the vapor chamber.
That vapor chamber itself has three times the surface area of the iPhone 17 Pro’s system. Apple claims the combination delivers up to 40% better sustained performance, which should be most noticeable during gaming, video work and intensive on-device AI rather than ordinary web browsing and messaging.


						

							


RAM: How much memory does the iPhone 18 Pro/Max have?
Apple does not officially publish RAM capacities for iPhones, and its launch material does not specify a RAM figure.
Reports ahead of the event indicated 12GB of RAM, but importantly the iPhone 17 Pro was also widely reported to have 12GB. That means there may not be a capacity increase this generation.
The more important confirmed improvement is 50% higher memory bandwidth, which allows the A20 Pro, GPU and Neural Engine to access data faster.
That is particularly relevant to Apple Intelligence and Siri AI. Larger on-device AI models demand not only sufficient RAM but very high memory bandwidth, so Apple’s chip and packaging changes should allow more complex models to run locally and for longer without the same thermal constraints.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max connectivity options 
C2 modem
One of the biggest changes is Apple’s C2 cellular modem, replacing the Qualcomm modem used in the previous Pro generation.
Apple says C2 delivers:
Faster upload performance than C1X
15% lower energy consumption
AI-powered improvements to connection quality and reliability
mmWave support in the U.S.
This confirms a major rumor from before the launch.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
Like the predecessors, the 2026 iPhones use Apple’s N1 wireless networking chip, supporting:
Wi-Fi 7
Bluetooth 6
Thread
Satellite
Emergency SOS via satellite, Messages via satellite, Roadside Assistance via satellite and Find My satellite functionality continue. Apple made no announcements about full satellite internet or ordinary 5G data delivered by satellite, despite pre-launch rumors suggesting such a capability could appear.


						

							


iPhone 18 Pro/Max Battery, MagSafe and charging: What’s changed?
Battery life is one of the most significant improvements.
Apple says eSIM-only models gain additional battery capacity because the space previously occupied by the physical SIM tray can be used for battery cells. Physical-SIM variants provide around two hours less video playback than equivalent eSIM-only models.
The improvement comes from a combination of larger batteries, the more efficient 2nm A20 Pro processor and lower-power C2 modem.


						

							




Apple rates eSIM-only models for up to:


ModeliPhone 18iPhone 17Improvement
Pro36 hours video playback33 hoursUp to +3 hours
Pro Max45 hours video playback39 hours+6 hours

 






Wired charging
Wired charging is faster. The iPhone 18 Pro can reach 50% in around 15 minutes, compared with around 20 minutes for the iPhone 17 Pro. Five minutes of wired charging can provide around seven hours of video playback on the Pro Max.
MagSafe and wireless charging
Wireless charging can reach 50% in around 30 minutes, which is broadly unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro generation. There is therefore a wired-charging speed improvement, but Apple hasn’t announced a comparable jump in MagSafe charging speed.


						

							




iPhone 18 Pro price: How much does it cost?
Apple has increased prices by $100 in the U.S. and £100 in the U.K. 
The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199/£1,199, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299/£1,299. Both begin with 256GB of storage.


ModeliPhone 18 starting priceiPhone 17 starting priceChange
iPhone Pro$1,199/£1,199$1,099/£1,099+$100/£100
iPhone Pro Max$1,299/£1,299$1,199/£1,199+$100/£100

 



Apple offers both models with 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB. That means the entry-level storage remains 256GB rather than increasing again. The notable change is that 2TB is now available on both models; previously the iPhone 17 Pro topped out at 1TB while the Pro Max could be configured with 2TB.
The $100 increase is considerably smaller than some analyst predictions before launch. Those forecasts had pointed to sharply higher DRAM and NAND costs caused by the global memory shortage, with estimates that the cost of 12GB of DRAM alone could rise dramatically this year. That makes component and memory pricing a credible contributor to Apple’s increase, although Apple itself hasn’t attributed the higher price to any one component.
Should you buy the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max? Which model should you choose?

				
					

				
			
Which one do you want?

Apple




The iPhone 18 Pro is a much stronger upgrade than the specifications initially suggest. The variable-aperture camera, A20 Pro, improved cooling, faster charging and better battery life all make meaningful differences, particularly for photography, gaming and intensive AI use. iPhone 17 Pro owners don’t need to rush to upgrade unless those features matter, but anyone coming from an iPhone 15 Pro or older will see a substantial jump. The 6.3-inch Pro is the better choice for most buyers because it has the same cameras and processor. Choose the Pro Max mainly if you want its larger display and class-leading 45-hour video battery life.

title: Siri on Apple Watch can remember useful parts of your day without retaining everything
content:
Your Apple Watch now listens all day to build a daily Siri Recap from the sounds around you. The catch? It actually forgets the audio the moment it understands the context.

Siri Recap
Audio Intelligence uses Sound Recognition to identify relevant information from the wearer's surroundings as events happen. Siri can combine those signals with other available data to summarize the day later.
Sound Recognition can identify events such as sirens, alarms, doorbells, and a crying baby, giving the system potential safety and accessibility uses. A separate Live Rewind feature lets users double-press the Digital Crown to replay the previous 15 seconds of detected audio and view a transcript.
The resulting Siri Recap doesn't include transcripts of overheard conversations, and Apple says the feature doesn't store audio. Sound processing happens continuously before the original audio is discarded.

title: Apple Reference Image is a new way to authenticate iPhone photography
content:
Apple Reference Image gives iPhone 18 Pro owners verifiable evidence of what the camera captured, offering a new defense against convincing AI-generated and edited images.

Apple Reference Image
The opt-in feature uses a new sensor in the Main camera that can sign every pixel it sees. Taking a photo in Reference mode captures signed sensor data that Private Cloud Compute turns into an unalterable reference image.
The Photos app displays that reference beside the main photo like a digital negative, allowing viewers to compare the two and determine whether edits were made. Apple's official release says the feature is designed for photojournalists, photographers, and everyday viewers.
Apple Reference Image first appeared in beta code in August. Apple has now confirmed that APIs in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 will let third-party apps display reference images.

title: Apple Announces Foldable 'iPhone Duo'
content:
Apple today announced the "iPhone Duo," a new kind of iPhone featuring two screens and a foldable inner display.


The two halves of the iPhone Duo connect into a single continuous frame with the same aspect ratio across both displays, and Apple said the transition between open and closed is designed to feel fluid. When fully open, Apple called it the thinnest iPhone ever made, with an architecture that packages its components into the camera plateau. 

Touch ID is built into the side button, and the device can also be unlocked using an Apple Watch.

A custom hinge, made from more than 100 tiny precision components, holds the display flat when open and controls the folding motion. Apple said the structure uses a multi layer lamination design with viscoelastic adhesives that let the display's layers glide against each other during folding "like pages in a book," preventing distortion over time. A titanium plate forms the bottom layer for added durability, with carbon fiber support plates creating a stiff, lightweight base for the display to rest on.



iPhone 18 Pro Max and 80% larger than the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, while the outer display is 5.4 inches and offers 90% of the screen area of the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌. Apple Pencil support is coming to both displays later this year.

For the display surface itself, Apple said it created a custom nano texture finish that cuts down on glare and reflections. The company also described a separate micro lens texture, produced using maskless laser lithography that writes each lens pixel by pixel, which it said creates a "perceptually flat matte surface" that minimizes the visibility of the fold crease while still feeling premium to the touch.

Home Screen dock is now oriented vertically, and the status bar has been redesigned to fit into the corner of the display. Software transitions gracefully between the outer and inner displays as the device opens, with controls staying in a consistent position while content scales up.

iOS also adapts to how the device is angled or propped, and it can be used partially folded, with content sliding away from the crease where taps are harder to register. Custom audio tuning adjusts for the changing distance between the speakers depending on how the device is positioned. Users can run two apps at once or open the same app twice, and can swipe up from the bottom to switch apps or pair two apps together to reopen later. A new Standby mode adds widgets for music, calendar, or weather, and Apple said the device can double as a bedside clock with a soft glow. 

The iPhone Duo uses the same 48MP Fusion main camera design Apple has used elsewhere in its lineup alongside a 48MP Fusion ultra wide camera, the same ultra wide used in the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, and supports Apple's upgraded Photographic Styles. Since the device can stand on its own, Apple said it opens up new options for capturing time lapses in 4K Dolby Vision HDR.

FaceTime camera hidden behind the screen, which works whether the device is fully open or propped on a surface, and the two cameras can dual capture front and rear scenes simultaneously. A new Duo ‌FaceTime‌ feature lets someone else join a video call from the outer display. A Smart Take feature tracks a scene and automatically takes the photo once everyone in a group shot is ready, removing the need to set a timer, and the outer display can play animations to help hold a child's attention for the camera.

iPhone 17 Pro. The iPhone Duo is eSIM only worldwide.

Each half of the device has its own battery, which Apple said operate together as a single battery for all day use, rated at up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner display and 44 hours on the outer display. Using both screens equally, Apple rates the device for up to 24 hours of battery life, with fast charging reaching 50% in around 20 minutes and just five minutes of charging providing up to five hours of video playback on the outer display.

New accessories include a Duo Folio case with a built in kickstand, along with an iPhone Duo case made of two separate parts that wrap around each half of the device.

The iPhone Duo starts at $1,999 for 256GB, with storage options going up to 2TB. Preorders begin October 16, with availability starting October 23.

More to follow...

title: Apple Announces Apple Watch Ultra 4 With Two-Day Battery Life and Upgraded Health Tracking
content:
Apple today announced the Apple Watch Ultra 4, featuring a new S11 chip, a redesigned health sensing system, and a larger battery that Apple says delivers two days of battery life.


With improved power efficiency, Ultra 4 offers up to 18 hours of workout tracking with full GPS and heart rate monitoring, or 45 hours in its maximum extended workout mode. It comes in Black and Natural titanium, alongside new band colors and a new titanium Hermès band.

The redesigned health sensing system features a larger electrode surface for improved skin contact during ECG readings, photodiodes arranged in a ring to capture light more efficiently, and larger, more power-efficient green LEDs for heart rate tracking.

More frequent readings are displayed in an updated Heart Rate app and new watch face complications. Apple says the system delivers the most accurate heart rate tracking of any wearable, citing a study involving hundreds of participants running, cycling, and performing HIIT workouts, with an ECG chest strap used as the reference.


A new Readiness feature analyzes recent activity, vitals, and sleep each morning to provide a score indicating whether users should recover, pace themselves, or take on more activity.

Apple is also redesigning the Health app to offer personalized guidance powered by Apple Intelligence. A new Health Age feature combines Apple Watch metrics such as VO2 max and sleep with blood test biomarkers to compare users' health indicators with their chronological age. A Longevity tab brings together insights across sleep, movement, heart health, and other areas.


Users can enter lab results manually or sync their medical records. In the U.S., Apple will also offer access to a Quest blood panel covering more than 50 biomarkers for $119. A new VO2 max test uses the iPhone's camera alongside Apple Watch to assess users as they perform a series of exercises, providing immediate results. The redesigned Health app is coming later this year.

The S11 chip's energy-efficient always-on processor enables new Audio Intelligence features. Sound Recognition identifies sounds such as alarms, doorbells, and a baby crying, while Live Rewind displays a transcript of what was said in the preceding 15 seconds.


Siri Recap generates titles, summaries, and key points from conversations for users to review in the Siri app. Users can schedule when it takes notes or toggle it in Control Center. Apple says the audio features do not create or store audio recordings. Siri Recap will launch in beta later this year, initially in English, with additional languages to follow.

title: Apple's A20 Pro is 40% faster, and offers improved thermal management
content:
Apple's iPhone 18 Pro offers a redesigned thermal system that's much larger and much better at dissipating heat generated by the powerful A20 Pro chip.


Apple's A20 Pro chip utilizes a new packaging method.
The A20 Pro features a six-core CPU with two super cores that are up to 20% faster, along with four efficiency cores. There's also a seven-core GPU for faster graphics rendering, offering up to a 40% increase in performance over the A19 Pro, along with a dual Neural Engine setup.
Apple has also redesigned the physical package of the silicon for the A20 Pro chip. Custom packaging, inspired by M-series chips, means that the A20 Pro silicon die is located side-by-side with the memory. Apple says this removes the memory from the thermal path of the system-on-chip and allows the chip to be connected directly to the improved vapor chamber.

title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max Guide: Everything you need to know about the new iPhones
content:
Macworld






Apple is unveiling the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at an event. We are updating this article as the news breaks! 
New iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max features at a glance
A20 Pro performance: New six-core CPU with two “super cores” up to 20% faster, upgraded GPU, and neural accelerators with 2x faster 8-bit floating-point AI performance.
Much better cooling: A next-generation vapor chamber is three times larger than the iPhone 17 Pro’s and circulates deionized water to improve thermals.
Big battery gains: Apple claims up to 36 hours for iPhone 18 Pro and 45 hours for iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Improved 48MP camera: Variable aperture opens wider in low light, letting in around 50% more light and improving Night mode speed and quality.
Higher prices: iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, while iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299, both $100 more than their predecessors.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Mac use the A20 Pro chip which has Apple’s latest six core CPU featuring two of our new super cores that are up to 20% faster and four efficiency cores, all integrated with neural accelerators that power low latency on device AI workloads as a significantly advanced GPU and a new version of the neural accelerators with 2x faster 8-bit floating point math. 
To keep cool, the iPhone 18 Pro has a next generation vapor chamber. It has three times the surface area as the one in iPhone 17 Pro. Deionized water is constantly cycled throughout the system for significantly improved thermals. 
Combined with the new chip’s efficiency, you’ll get 36 hours on the iPhone 18 Pro and an absolutely insane 45 hours on the 18 Pro Max. 
The 48MP Fusion Camera with variable aperture adjusts automatically based on the scene. When you’re in a darker environment, the aperture opens to let in around 50% more light, while night mode captures are faster with better quality.
The iPhone 18 Pro will cost from $1,199 (up from $1,099) while the the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,299 (up from $1,199 for the iPhone 17 Pro Max).
The new iPhone 18 Pro also has a smaller Dynamic Island with space for three Live Activities at once, a large one in the middle and two smaller circles on either side. 
Read on to see the rumors from before the event while we update this article. 
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch at an Apple event on September 9, 2026 featuring several cutting-edge hardware advancements, including the debut of Apple’s C2 modem, and a shift to a 2nm manufacturing process for the A20 Pro chip. 
Other key rumored upgrades include a smaller Dynamic Island that will allow users to switch between three Live Activities at the top of the screen, rather than the two supported by current iPhones. While under-display Face ID components and camera improvements may include variable aperture on the Pro Max and enhanced sensors.
Alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max Apple is said to be planning to launch the ultra-premium folding iPhone – which it turns out could be called iPhone Duo. However, in a change to the usual schedule, the company is expected to shift the launch of the iPhone 18 spring 2027 to keep the spotlight on the Pro series during its traditional September debut.
Here’s a quick summary of what all the rumors and leaks say to expect from the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in 2026.


What are the biggest upgrades for iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max
Unveiling at Apple’s September 9 event
Smaller Dynamic Island, potentially with some Face ID components under the display
Variable-aperture main camera
A20 Pro chip built on TSMC’s 2nm process
Apple C2 cellular modem
New N2 wireless/networking chip
Larger battery, particularly on the Pro Max
Simplified Camera Control
Revised, more seamless rear Ceramic Shield design
Possible 5G satellite connectivity
Likely price increase due to soaring memory and component costs
How is iPhone 18 Pro/Max different from iPhone 17 Pro/Max?
Split release schedule (Pro first, base later)
Smaller or modified Dynamic Island
Some Face ID components moving under-display
New C2 modem 
Camera experimentation (rumored variable aperture on Pro Max)

 Comparing iPhone 18 Pro rumors to current iPhone 17 Pro






When will the new iPhones launch?
Apple has confirmed that it will hold an event on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, and new iPhones are highly likely to headline the event.
However, Apple is widely expected to change its usual release strategy this year. Multiple reports suggest suggest that only the premium models will arrive in September 2026: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a new foldable iPhone Ultra. 
The standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e and a second generation iPhone Air are instead expected in spring 2027. If accurate, this would represent the biggest shake-up to Apple’s iPhone launch schedule in years, creating separate autumn and spring release windows.
Evidence in iOS 27 beta 5 adds weight to those reports. System files reportedly reference six unreleased iPhones: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and foldable iPhone Ultra. The references don’t reveal specifications, but they support the idea that Apple is preparing all six models while staggering their release dates. 
Availability could also be a problem. During Apple’s Q3 earnings call, then-CEO Tim Cook, now executive chairman, warned that the impact of supply constraints would “increase significantly.”
Apple is reportedly struggling to secure enough DRAM for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra, potentially limiting production ahead of launch. Processor wafers are said to be ready, but some are reportedly waiting for memory before they can be packaged and assembled.
That could leave the iPhone 18 Pro in short supply when it goes on sale, with longer shipping estimates possible. The lower-volume iPhone Ultra may be somewhat less affected.
Most likely: The iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and foldable iPhone Ultra will launch in September 2026, while the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 will follow in early 2027.

What will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max look like and what are the color choices?
The design of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max is said to resemble the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, but some changes are predicted.
One possible change, shared by a Weibo leaker in September 2025, is a “slightly transparent” ceramic shield section on the back of Pro models. This glass/Ceramic Shield area around MagSafe is now rumored to become more frosted and visually seamless. 
Macworld contributor Filipe Esposito reported that a trusted source had revealed one of the new colorways for the iPhone 18 Pro to be Dark Cherry, replacing the iPhone 17 Pro’s Cosmic Orange option.
Recent rumors claimed that the new phones will be significantly thicker than previous models, but all the evidence we have seen says that’s not the case, including case maker Otter Box confidently listing their iPhone 17 Pro cases as fitting the iPhone 18 Pro. Instead, we expect the body to have about the same thickness as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max but with a thicker camera bump area.
Another report suggests that the Camera Control on the side of the iPhone will be pressure sensing instead of a touch-sensing layer. This redesign is said to be aimed at reducing the cost and complexity.  
A recent ransomware attack against an Apple parts supplier included images from an iPhone 18 Pro “drop test” and other parts, and they corroborate prior rumors about the overall shape and design of the phone, which is broadly the same as the iPhone 17 Pro.
Other shades are said to include: Light Blue, Dark Gray, and Silver. There was also a coffee shade rumored (via Digital Chat Station).

iPhone 18 Pro colors revealed! #iphone #apple
 ♬ original sound – Macworld – Macworld 
  




As with the iPhone 17 Pro, there will be no black option, according to Instant Digital.
Screen sizes are expected to remain at 6.3 and 6.9 inches. The Pro models will also retain the wider three-camera raised plateau.
If you are hoping for a more dramatic redesign, the iPhone Ultra may have more appeal. Alternatively, you could wait for the 20th anniversary iPhone which is rumored to have a “radically different design“. Reports point to a curved, near-bezel-free display, possible solid-state haptic buttons, a thinner and brighter OLED panel, and potentially under-display Face ID and camera hardware coming in fall 2027.
Most likely: Design changes will be minimal, with the biggest visible differences limited to colors and subtle refinements.


						

							


What’s new with the iPhone 18 Pro/Max camera?

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




Apple may introduce variable aperture technology to the 48MP main camera on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (potentially only the Pro Max), allowing mechanical control over light intake and depth of field. This has long been a perk limited to high-end professional cameras.
If the rumor (from Digital Chat Station on Weibo), and later corroborated by Mark Gurman on September 9, is true, iPhone users will be able to mechanically control how much light reaches the sensor for the first time, allowing more control over depth of field and sharpness. This could elevate portrait shots by improving the applied depth of field effect, as well as minimizing overexposure.
Wider telephoto apertures on the Pro models should also result in better low-light performance.
For some time (since January 2025) Samsung has been said to be working on a new three-layer stacked camera sensor called ‘PD-TR-Logic,’ and this could appear in the iPhone 18 series. This image sensor is expected to enhance the camera’s responsiveness, while also offering advantages such as reduced photo noise, improved dynamic range. The main Wide camera sensor is expected to be larger than usual, which offers many benefits.
The front-facing camera may also get an upgrade beyond the rumored changes to the housing (as discussed elsewhere the selfie camera may be housed in a smaller hole-punch cut out, reducing the size of the Dynamic Island). The iPhone 17 generation features 18MP sensors for the selfie camera, but this may increase to 24MP in the next generation, according to leaker WhyLab on Weibo.
More megapixels would lead to improved video calls and better low-light performance. 
Most likely: Incremental improvements, with a new variable aperture feature on the Pro Max.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max Dynamic Island or front camera change?

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle




Apple hasn’t changed the Dynamic Island since the iPhone 14 Pro, but the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce some adjustments.
Some reports suggest Apple could move certain Face ID components under the display, allowing the Dynamic Island to shrink. This is not expected to mean that the entire Face ID system will be hidden beneath the screen. 
A report in December 2025 from Weibo account “Smart Pikachu” claimed that Apple was testing an under-display “micro-transparent glass panel” for some Face ID sensors. That could allow Apple to reduce the size of the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 Pro.
Later reports, however, suggest that full under-display Face ID is not expected yet. Instead, Apple may move only some of the sensors or emitters used by Face ID beneath the display, while other components remain visible within a smaller Dynamic Island.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has also reported that Apple plans to “shrink” the Dynamic Island on future iPhone models, adding weight to the idea that Apple is redesigning or relocating some of the components currently housed within it.
On the morning of September 9, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman published a report claiming that the smaller Dynamic Island will let users toggle between three live tasks, versus the current limit of two Live Activities.
A spy shot published in March by noted leaker IceUniverse on X gives us a view of how much smaller the Dynamic Island could be.

				
					

				
			
IceUniverse/X




There have been conflicting claims that the position of the front-facing camera may also change: 
In December 2025 The Information claimed Apple will put the Face ID sensors under the display, and move the front camera to the upper left corner in a punch-hole design. This would make the iPhone 18 Pro/ Max the first iPhones with a front camera in the corner.
However, Prominent leaker account Instant Digital said on Weibo in January 2026 that front camera claim was based on a mistranslation, and only the infrared sensor moves under the display. Leakers ShrimpApplePro and Ross Young of DSCC corroborated Instant Digital’s claims.
Most likely: A smaller Dynamic Island, with some Face ID hardware moved under the display, rather than fully under-display Face ID.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max display change?

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




Screen sizes should be consistent with the 6.3 and 6.9-inch displays on the current models, but reports suggest a massive jump in brightness from the current 1600 nits HDR and 3,000 nits peak. 
According to Weibo leaker, Instant Digital, Chinese supplier BOE has revealed that Apple is targeting unprecedentedly high brightness requirements for the display. The Elec corroborated this, claiming BOE is struggling with iPhone OLED production so panel orders have been shifted to Samsung Display.
Most likely: An increase in brightness is expected, but there are no details yet on the extent of the improvement.


						

							


How powerful will the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro/Max be?
The iPhone 18 Pro and Max are expected to use a new A20 Pro chip, built on TSMC’s N2 (2nm) process. The move to a smaller manufacturing process should allow Apple to pack in more transistors, with TSMC claiming up to 15% better performance or 30% lower power consumption compared with its previous-generation technology.
A September 2026 leak suggests the A20 Pro could feature a 7-core GPU, up from six cores in the A19 Pro, while retaining a six-core CPU with two performance and four efficiency cores.
Perhaps more significant is the rumored move to a 96-bit LPDDR5x memory interface, 50% wider than the A19 Pro’s 64-bit interface. Combined with possible clock-speed and architectural improvements, we estimate that GPU performance could rise by around 20–30%, benefiting local AI workloads, 3D games and other graphics-intensive apps.
The A20 is also rumored to use Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging, integrating the RAM more closely with the SoC. That could improve memory bandwidth and latency, while potentially reducing power consumption.
Apple could also borrow ideas from its M-series chips, with speculation that the A20 may introduce higher-performance “super cores” similar to those used in the M5.
Apple introduced vapor-chamber cooling with the iPhone 17 Pro generation, spreading heat away from the processor more efficiently than the older graphite-based system. Gurman’s report on the morning of September 9, referrs to an updated vapor chamber cooling system alongside the A20 Pro that should allow the A20 Pro sustain its performance without getting too hot. 
Most likely: A substantial underlying upgrade in performance, graphics and efficiency, although many of the improvements may be more noticeable in demanding games and AI features than in everyday use.


						

							


Will iPhone 18 Pro/Max battery life improve?
Apple works to make battery life as long as possible every year, especially in the Pro model iPhones. 
A July report claimed that the battery capacity of the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a battery capacity of 5,235 mAh on the Nano SIM model and 5,425 mAh on the eSIM-only version. That’s about 6-8% more capacity than the current model. Further reports have puts the U.S. eSIM iPhone 18 Pro Max at 5,567mAh. 
The “Pro Max” variant of the iPhone gets a higher-capacity battery nearly every year, usually a couple hundred mAh more, thanks to better internal design and improving battery chemistry and manufacturing techniques. But battery life is a function of more than just battery capacity—the power use of the processor, display, and wireless radios all play an important point.
We think it’s likely the iPhone 18 Pro/Max will have higher-capacity batteries, and battery life at least as long as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max. But a significantly longer battery life is hard to predict.


						

							


Will connectivity improve (5G, Wi-Fi, satellite) with iPhone 18 Pro/Max?
C2 and N2 chip rumors. 
iPhone 18 Pro models are rumored to feature the second generation of Apple’s in-house 5G modem, the C2 chip. 
The C2 hasn’t launched yet, but it is expected to replace Qualcomm modems in at least some iPhone 18 Pro models. Qualcomm hardware may still be used in certain markets, depending on regional and carrier requirements:
Better power efficiency
Faster and more reliable 5G performance
Improved mmWave support
There are also reports that the new iPhone will gain full satellite internet support, expanding beyond emergency use. In October 2025, The Information claimed that Apple is gearing up to support 5G networks that are served from satellites. 
While the iPhone has offered satellite connectivity for emergency situations for years, if this rumor is true it would allow the iPhone 18 models to have full internet access via satellite, not just emergency services.
As of April 2026, Apple and Amazon have agreed to team up to provide future satellite service support. Early in April, Amazon announced that it had agreed to acquire Globalstar, who was the provider of iPhone and Apple Watch satellite connectivity (that merger is expected to close in 2027) So now iPhones and Apple Watches will now fall under Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite internet network.
The Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip is less certain. Apple debuted its N1 local networking chip in the iPhone 17 line, supporting Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread networking.
Earlier in 2026, analyst Jeff Pu said that the iPhone 18 Pro models will introduce a next-generation N2 chip, but leaks of a iPhone 18 Pro motherboard in July 2026 suggested Apple could retain the N1 for another generation. There is little information about what an N2 would add beyond the capabilities of the N1.
Most likely: An incremental upgrade to wireless performance, reliability and efficiency rather than a major new connectivity feature.


						

							


How much will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max cost?
With Apple increasing prices for Macs and iPads in June due to high memory and chip costs, and the iPhone 18 Pro models are also expected to become more expensive.
In August, Mark Gurman described iPhone price increases as “inevitable” as Apple faces rising memory and component costs. 
As of September 9, Gurman is reporting that Apple plans to increase both Pro models by $100.
A roughly $100 increase may be the most plausible outcome. Google and Samsung have both raised flagship prices by about $100, potentially setting a benchmark Apple may be reluctant to exceed. That could put the iPhone 18 Pro at around $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299.
Apple could also absorb some of the higher costs itself. Recent warnings about pressure on gross margins suggest the company may accept lower profitability rather than pass the full increase on to customers.
More pessimistic estimates are higher. IDC has suggested increases of up to $200 for the Pro models, while analyst Jeff Pu has indicated that prices could rise by as much as $250 to $300.
The rumored folding iPhone could further reshape the top end of Apple’s pricing, with reports suggesting a starting price of $1,999 or more.
Most likely: A price rise of around $100 for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, although larger increases remain possible if component costs stay elevated.

 FAQ 


1.
When is the new iPhone coming out?
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to be unveiled at Apple’s September 9, 2026 event, with preorders likely shortly afterward (estimates suggest September 12) and availability around mid-September (estimates suggest September 18). The standard iPhone 18, however, is expected to arrive in spring 2027.





2.
Will the iPhone 18 Pro have under-display Face ID?
Probably not fully. Current rumors suggest the iPhone 18 Pro may move some Face ID components beneath the display, allowing Apple to shrink the Dynamic Island. However, the complete Face ID system is not expected to go under-display yet.





3.
What chip will power the iPhone 18 Pro?
Apple is expected to use the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro.





4.
Is Apple changing its iPhone release schedule in 2026?
Apple is said to be planning to launch the Pro iPhone models, including a foldable iPhone in September 2026. The iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e may not arrive until spring 2027. 





5.
What camera upgrades are rumored for the iPhone 18 Pro Max?
Apple is rumored to be focusing on advanced lens technology and sensor improvements for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. One prominent rumor is the introduction of a variable-aperture system in the Pro Max.

title: AirPods 5 Announced With Improved Noise Cancellation, Audio Quality, and More
content:
Apple today introduced AirPods 5, bringing Active Noise Cancellation to its entry-level wireless earbuds at a starting price of $129.

 
Apple says AirPods 5 remove up to 50% more external noise than AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation. A redesigned acoustic architecture and updated Adaptive EQ also promise richer, more detailed sound, while an improved Transparency mode makes nearby voices and sounds more natural.

Both models include Adaptive Audio, which automatically blends noise cancellation and Transparency mode, and Conversation Awareness, which lowers playback volume when the wearer starts speaking. Live Translation is also supported when paired with a compatible iPhone with Apple Intelligence enabled.

A $149 version with a Wireless Charging Case adds swipe-based volume controls on the stems and longer battery life. Apple says this model delivers up to five hours of listening with noise cancellation enabled, or up to 22 hours with the case, which supports Apple Watch and Qi chargers alongside USB-C.

title: Both iPhone 18 Pro Models Feature Variable Aperture Camera
content:
Apple has revealed at its "Surprise and Shine" event that both iPhone 18 Pro models will be equipped with a variable aperture camera.


Prior to this announcement, some rumours suggested that only the iPhone 18 Pro Max would feature a variable aperture lens, but it seems that both models will benefit from the technology.

Apple says it has developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair, to create the aperture lens. The blades are made of a specialized polymer composite for the right balance of mass flexibility and durability.

The aperture adjusts automatically based on the scene. When you're in a darker environment, for example, the aperture opens to let in around 50% more light.

It also allows you to capture cinematic mode effects from regular video after you capture, plus it now supports 60 frames per second for a half-speed effect.

"iPhone 18 Pro has a new 48 megapixel fusion main camera with variable aperture for creative control that wasn't possible before," said Apple. "This is the most advanced camera we've ever made."

title: Apple Unveils A20 Pro as First 2nm Smartphone Chip
content:
Apple today revealed the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, built on a brand new architecture using 2nm process technology.


Apple described the A20 Pro as "an exceptional chip that sets a new bar for mobile computing." The chip has a 6-core CPU design with two new super cores that Apple says are up to 20% faster, calling them "desktop class" and "the fastest in any smartphone," alongside four new efficiency cores.

The GPU has also been redesigned with a 7-core layout that Apple says delivers up to 40% faster graphics performance and increased memory bandwidth. New neural accelerators built into the GPU offer twice the FP8 performance of the previous generation, which helps the chip run large language models locally on the device.

The A20 Pro features an additional Neural Engine, bringing the total core count to 32. The company says the redesigned Neural Engine delivers 2x the compute of its predecessor, is more efficient, and now supports 8-bit floating point math. Apple called the A20 Pro "the ultimate chip for running advanced on-device models," adding that it ships with "the widest memory interface we've ever shipped in an iPhone."

The company said effective thermal management in the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ is critical to unlocking the chip's maximum performance, since efficient heat dissipation determines how much of that performance can be sustained. To support this, Apple redesigned the chip's silicon packaging, describing it as "custom packaging inspired by our M-series chips" that connects the silicon and memory directly to the vapor chamber for improved thermal performance.

iPhone 17 Pro, and twice the sustained performance compared to the A18 Pro chip in the iPhone 16 Pro.

title: Apple Announces iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max
content:
Apple today unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which look very similar to the iPhone 17 Pro models but have several upgrades.


iPhone 18 Pro still has a 6.3-inch display, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max sticks with a 6.9-inch display. As was widely rumored, both devices have a smaller Dynamic Island that can show up to three Live Activities at once.

The devices are equipped with the A20 Pro chip and feature longer battery life. Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro matches the battery life of the iPhone 17 Pro Max with up to 24 hours of typical usage per full charge, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max has the biggest generational leap in battery life ever with up to 30 hours of usage per charge.

Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro can charge to 50% in just 15 minutes.

A20 Pro has a 6-core GPU, a 7-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. Apple says sustained performance is up to 40% faster compared to the A19 Pro chip.

The vapor chamber cooling system is three times as large in the iPhone 18 Pro models as it is in the iPhone 17 Pro models for improved thermal management.

Six laser-cut blades smoothly transition between different apertures, making it incredibly easy to capture the best shot by automatically adjusting for depth of field and lighting. Combined with a new sensor that improves image quality, the result is better low-light photography, crisper detail in the back of group photos, and more unique shots.
With a new computational imaging pipeline, Apple says the Main camera produces sharper, more detailed shots, while upgraded Photographic Styles with new texture and grain controls let users further dial in their desired appearance.

iPhone 18 Pro color options include Black, Silver, Glacier, and Burgundy. The rear aluminum and Ceramic Shield glass area are now more color matched.

In the U.S., the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at $1,299. For the first time, a 2TB storage capacity is available.

title: Mac Mini vs. Mac Studio Buyer's Guide: 20 Differences Compared
content:
Apple announced new Mac mini and Mac Studio models last month, with both available to pre-order now. It is the first time in years that Apple has revised its two desktop Macs simultaneously, so which should you choose?


There are now two desktop Macs to choose from following the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, but the prices have moved sharply. The ‌Mac Studio‌ starts at $2,499 and rises to $5,499 for the M5 Ultra model, while the ‌Mac mini‌ starts at $899 with the M6 chip and $1,699 with the M5 Pro.

iPad increases Apple made in June, which took the ‌Mac mini‌ from $599 to $799, the M4 Pro configuration from $1,399 to $1,599, and the ‌Mac Studio‌ from $1,999 to $2,499. The M5 Ultra adds a further $200 to the post-June M3 Ultra price, putting it $1,500 above what the M3 Ultra cost at launch.

Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two desktop Macs is best for you. The two machines now share a large number of key features, including:
 

A boxy silver aluminum enclosure with no color options

Apple's N1 chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 to both machines for the first time

Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core

Hardware-accelerated ray tracing

A Media Engine with hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, plus AV1 decode

A next-generation SSD architecture that Apple says is up to twice as fast as before

Genlock support over USB-C for synchronizing a display with a camera, including the iPhone 17 Pro

An HDMI port with multichannel audio output

A 3.5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones



Beyond that, the two lines diverge on chip generation, memory capacity, ports, and external display support.

Both enclosures carry over unchanged, so the dimensions of the two devices remain radically different, with the ‌Mac Studio‌ dwarfing the ‌Mac mini‌ in every way.

Most customers should choose the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ over the M5 Max ‌Mac Studio‌, saving $800 on the base models. The gap widens across custom configurations, since the ‌Mac Studio‌'s memory and storage tiers start higher and climb further.
 
Apple's first 2nm chip. Its Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says system frameworks can drive simultaneously, is also more Neural Engine hardware than either the M5 Pro or the M5 Max provides. If your workload leans on on-device machine learning rather than sustained CPU or GPU throughput, the cheapest Mac in this comparison is not obviously the weakest one for the task. The trade-offs are Thunderbolt 4 rather than Thunderbolt 5, a 32GB memory and 2TB storage ceiling, and a single video encode engine.
 
M5 Ultra is Apple's first quad-die M-series chip, and its four ProRes engines, four video encode engines, and 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth are aimed squarely at multi-stream video work and large local AI models. The 512GB memory ceiling has no equivalent anywhere else in the Mac lineup, and it is what allows models with hundreds of billions of parameters to run entirely on device.
 
The ‌Mac Studio‌ still has a superior selection of ports, with four rear Thunderbolt 5 ports on the M5 Max and six in total on the M5 Ultra, plus an SDXC card slot, USB-A, and 10Gb Ethernet as standard. This makes a practical difference for anyone working off fast external storage or camera media. The ‌Mac mini‌ has closed part of the distance by moving to 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard, up from Gigabit.

Clustering over Thunderbolt 5 and RDMA is not a point of difference between the two machines, since it arrived in macOS 26.2 last December and works on any Mac with Thunderbolt 5, including the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ and the previous-generation ‌Mac Studio‌. The exception is the M6 ‌Mac mini‌, which has Thunderbolt 4 and cannot take part.
 
reach 165Hz at 4K, up from 144Hz on the M4 generation, and the M5 Pro model drives all three through a single Thunderbolt port. For a three-display desk setup at high refresh rates, the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ is sufficient. It is only above three displays, or at 6K and 8K, that the ‌Mac Studio‌ becomes necessary.
 
A notable exception arises at the top of the ‌Mac mini‌ lineup. An M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ configured with additional memory and storage moves close enough to the $2,499 ‌Mac Studio‌ that the comparison changes somewhat. For an increment of a few hundred dollars, the ‌Mac Studio‌ substitutes a chip with roughly twice the memory bandwidth, a second video encode engine, far greater display support, and headroom to 128GB of unified memory. If you are already spending heavily on a ‌Mac mini‌, price the ‌Mac Studio‌ before committing.
 
If you plan to keep the machine for many years, the ‌Mac Studio‌'s ceiling matters more than its starting price, because it is the only one of the two that can be configured beyond 64GB of unified memory. Buyers weighing the M6 ‌Mac mini‌ against the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ should note that the newer chip generation and the newer process node both sit in the cheaper machine, and that the M5 Pro's advantages are concentrated in multi-core and graphics performance rather than in longevity.
 
Studio Display, which starts from $1,599 and was one of the few products spared June's price rises. An M6 ‌Mac mini‌ paired with a ‌Studio Display‌ comes to $2,498, a dollar less than a bare M5 Max ‌Mac Studio‌ with nothing to plug into. An M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ and a ‌Studio Display‌ together come to $3,298, which is $799 more than the base ‌Mac Studio‌ and $2,201 less than the M5 Ultra ‌Mac Studio‌ with no display at all.

title: Apple Event Today: 20 Last-Minute 'iPhone Duo' and iPhone 18 Pro Rumors
content:
Apple will be holding an event today starting at 10 a.m. Pacific Time, with the company expected to unveil its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, AirPods 5, and potentially more. Below, we have recapped 20 last-minute rumors about these devices.


All of the details below were reported by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman today.

Apple's foldable iPhone will be named iPhone Duo.

  
iPhone Duo will have Apple Pencil support.

  
iPhone Duo shipments to customers will begin as early as October. It is unclear if pre-orders will begin earlier.

  
iPhone Duo color options: white and dark blue.

  
iPhone Duo starts with 256GB of storage. U.S. pricing will start at around $1,999.

  
iPhone Duo will have Apple's A20 Pro chip and C2 modem for 5G.

  
iPhone Duo will have dual rear 48-megapixel cameras. No Telephoto camera.

  
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max special color: dark red.

  
iPhone 18 Pro models will have longer battery life — the Pro Max especially.

  
iPhone 18 Pro models will have an improved vapor chamber system to reduce overheating.

  
At least one iPhone 18 Pro model's camera will have variable aperture for greater control over depth of field.

  
In the U.S., iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max starting prices will be $100 higher compared to iPhone 17 Pro models. This means the iPhone 18 Pro would start at $1,199, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max would start at $1,299.

  
iPhone 18 Pro's smaller Dynamic Island can show three Live Activities, up from two.

  
Do not expect a regular iPhone 18 model to be announced today, as Apple reportedly plans to launch that device in the first quarter of 2027.

  
Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 models will have new case color options.

  
Apple Watch Series 12 will have a ceramic case option.

  
Apple Watch Ultra 4 will have longer battery life compared to the Ultra 3.

  
An all-new Readiness app for the Apple Watch will be announced today.

  
The new Apple Watch models will offer a new daily summary feature.

  
AirPods 5 will be unveiled today — with and without active noise cancellation.

Surprise and Shine iPhone event: How to watch

Surprise and Shine iPhone event: What we expect
Apple might have dubbed this the “Surprise” event, but we have a pretty good idea what Apple is going to announce. Here’s what we expect to see:
iPhone Ultra: Apple is almost certain to launch its first folding phone this week. We’re expecting a passport-style design with a 5.5-inch cover display and a near-8-inch inner display when opened.
iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: We expect a similar design with a faster chip and a better camera system, possibly including a variable-aperture lens for the first time.
Apple Watch Series 12: The latest Apple Watch update will reportedly be a minor refresh with a new chip, all-day heart-rate tracking, and maybe the return of a ceramic finish.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 is expected to be a minor refresh largely focused on a new chip tuned for Siri AI.
AirPods 5: Apple is rumored to be launching a new pair of low-end AirPods, but we don’t know much about them.
Smart home: It’s less likely that Apple’s rumored smart-home hub arrives at this event, but we could see an updated Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini.

It’s flies in the face of Apple’s pursuit of perfection and likely the reason why we haven’t gotten a folding iPhone until now.
Earlier this year, it was reported that Apple had devised a way to overcome the crease with a combination of ultra-thin glass (UTG) and an optically clear adhesive that allows “the folding area to be locally thinned at the bending axis to improve bendability.” Samsung’s newest flagship phone features a display with a 60-micrometer UTG layer, which is likely a similar material to what Apple will use.

title: The folding iPhone will support Apple Pencil after all, sources claim
content:
Macworld





A week or so ago, the Bloomberg leaker Mark Gurman made a bold claim: Apple had, “with zero doubt,” been testing and prototyping a new, stubbier version of the Apple Pencil for its upcoming foldable iPhone. Considering that the company has sold phones for 19 years and styluses for 11 years but has never brought the two things together, this seemed surprising. Some might even say a colossal mistake. But at least the idea was just that: an idea, tested for a while and probably discarded.
But hang on for a minute, because today, at the very last minute, Gurman has posted another article about Apple’s Surprise and Shine press event. And he now insists that the folding iPhone (or iPhone Duo, as he’s now calling it) will indeed be compatible with the Apple Pencil.
It’s important to note that Gurman’s latest prediction, in his own words, is merely that the iPhone Duo will have “support for the Apple Pencil stylus.” If Apple still plans to launch a special edition of the stylus, he doesn’t mention this. From the sound of this the inclusion of Apple Pencil support would be very much optional; a nice-to-have rather than an integral feature. Which sounds like something nobody could be against, right?
Except the screen, which is already a source of concern because of the dangers of a visible crease, will need the additional tech to support stylus input, and as Gurman himself has pointed out, that could result in visible marks. And the iPhone Ultra/Duo won’t be the right size for a standard-issue Apple Pencil to attach magnetically along one side, which creates all sorts of storage and charging headaches. All this to support an accessory most people won’t use.
To be fair, the foldable iPhone, when unfolded, will be more akin to a tablet than a smartphone. (Its expected screen size is virtually identical to the original iPad mini.) So there may be some demand for stylus support. It’s just hard to feel positive about what seems like a half-hearted approach to the matter. Either you do Apple Pencil support properly, with a dedicated version of the stylus that actually fits, or you don’t bother.
Then again, the Pencil gets the briefest of snippets in Gurman’s report, so perhaps there’s more to the story than he’s letting on. You can follow all the latest breaking news as we lead up to today’s announcement with our Apple event live blog.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Could Charge 25% Faster
content:
Code found in iOS 27 suggests the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max could support a 33% higher charging rate than the iPhone 17 Pro models, according to a new discovery from the leaker known as "pdfu."


The findings apparently come from Apple's charging optimizer settings buried in ‌iOS 27‌, which show the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max charging at a rate 33% higher than the iPhone 17 lineup. If Apple can maintain that higher rate throughout a charge, pdfu estimates it could cut around 25% off the time it takes to complete a typical fast-charging session.

Apple's first foldable iPhone does not appear to get the same treatment. The same code purportedly shows it charging at the same rate as the ‌iPhone 17‌ and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌, rather than the faster rate expected for the new Pro models.

iPhone 18 is said to match the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ faster charging, while the iPhone 18e is said to see an even bigger jump of around 69% over the current iPhone 17e. The iPhone Air 2 is said to charge about 27% faster than today's ‌iPhone Air‌.

Actual charging speeds depend on a multitude of real-world factors, such as the phone's temperature and how full the battery already is, so the improvement buyers notice day-to-day could end up being smaller than the numbers suggest.
